scope_choices: Automated model review, not independent human verification or empirical replication.
This synthesis read complete supplied text pages 1–10 and all supplied prior image-review notes. It did not receive or directly inspect raw page images.
The supplied PDF hash and page-call receipts were retained, not independently recomputed or authenticated.

All 128 feature definitions were considered; 131 feature assertions retain additional annotation-VLM, release-stage, and robustness-subfacet scopes. This is not a claim of machine-validated canonical admission.
No JSON Schema validator, semantic checker, graph builder, repository execution, external retrieval, or file write was run in this response.

The candidate's demonstrated L2 classification was not retained: persistent evolving state and action-conditioned transition evidence are partial. Core membership remains provisional/unresolved, not definitively excluded.

Block prediction need not be recursive to qualify under the ontology; the unresolved issue is whether the implemented scene representation is advanced over the procedural coordinate rather than merely retained as an appearance reference.

Complete temporal masks and optional target-aligned controls prescribe substantial future structure. Conditional synthesis must not be reinterpreted as autonomous forecasting from current information.
The evaluated clip length is 49 frames including I0, not an effective horizon. Cadence, elapsed duration, and error-versus-horizon tolerances are not reported.

R2 is restricted to visual-generation evaluation on actual held-out recorded surgical video. Patient/site independence, exact metric-specific generated sample counts, and video61–70's role are unresolved.
Depth, flow, edges, and descriptions are estimated annotations. Their adherence metrics do not establish physical geometry, tissue mechanics, contact validity, or surgical intervention effects.
Annotator count/qualifications/agreement, VLM identity/prompts, and description-validation procedures are not reported.
Baselines receive different supported inputs; strongest-baseline comparisons use different configurations across metrics and do not isolate an equal-information architecture effect.

Individual quality/adherence trade-offs are retained: full controls do not minimize Flow EPE; fixed-scale grounding and removal of anchor-relative modulation improve selected adherence metrics; direct summation leads Table V's three adherence metrics.

Confidence intervals, repeated-seed dispersion, statistical tests, uncertainty decomposition, calibration, first-frame evaluation exclusion, Figure 6 normalization, and Figure 8 aggregation are insufficiently reported or not reported.
Figure 7 repeats a baseline depth-error triplet across two conditioning columns. Values are preserved as reported pending clarification.
Manual mask curation is not a generated-output reader study. No actual clinical deployment, robot-control success, prospective system use, or patient/workflow benefit is established.
Extreme occlusion and rapid camera motion are author-reported challenges; explicit camera-motion modeling and long-horizon action conditioning are future work.
Code access, weights, licenses, derivative-data release, and external source details were not checked. Cited systems' capabilities and regulatory status are not inherited.
Legacy cells are preserved historical values, including unsupported positive/negative fields and prior audit descriptions. They do not override the qualified current assertions.
